timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna told me what happened in that room later. She told it sitting beside me with her bare feet under my leg, stopping whenever she wanted water and starting again wherever it hurt. I asked her the same questions until she threatened to throw the glass at me. Some parts she could give me word for word. Some parts she wouldn't give anybody.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: This is what she told me. Red took her back through the Saint after we'd gone, with two men behind her and one hand around her arm. The party hadn't completely emptied. A few people were still holding drinks because nobody had personally told them the good time was dead. She saw a woman by the elevators lift a phone.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Get my good side, Shawna said. Red pulled her harder. The woman lowered the phone. You always gotta do that? he asked. Look good? Make a fucking scene. You dragged me out of one. He took her into a private room she knew. White chairs. White carpet. A huge painting of a horse coming out of the ocean. Red loved that painting.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He'd once spent twenty minutes explaining the horse to her while she tried to work out whether she could leave without him noticing. Tonight the carpet had somebody else's blood on it. One of the men had brought her purse from the office. Red took it from him and put it on the table.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then he shut the door and told the men to wait outside. Shawna said that was when she first got scared enough to feel cold. Not at the gunfire. Not at his hand on her arm. At the little click of the door and the fact that he wanted no one else to hear him talk. Sit, he said. She stayed standing. Shawna.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Give me a cigarette. He went to the table and took one from a silver box. He lit it before he handed it to her, like he was bringing her flowers. I could've killed that nigga, he said. She took the cigarette. Nigga, you tried. Nigga ran. My nigga's coming back. Red laughed. They always come back for the money.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then put me outside and see. He didn't answer that. He poured a drink, missed the glass a little, and wiped the spill with his sleeve. Shawna noticed because Red never cleaned anything. He would wait for somebody to come across a whole room to pick up a thing beside his shoe. He was angry enough to forget who he thought he was.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You think that nigga loves you? She smoked. I asked you something. I heard you. That nigga loves winning. You're what he stole. Soon as you're just a woman in his house, watch what happens. She looked at the painting instead of him. The horse had its mouth open. She'd always thought it looked surprised to be swimming. He begged, you know, Red said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She kept looking at the horse. Dante. That nigga begged us to look after you. Us. Red stopped with the bottle in his hand. Shawna turned toward him. You were standing there? I didn't say that. Then who told you? He put the bottle down too carefully. Everybody knew what happened. I didn't. He looked toward the door. She watched him do it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna said she would've given anything to have the old letter and the order in her hand right then, to lay them in his lap and make him touch what he'd done. All she had was the watch. She turned it around her wrist. What did he call me? she asked. What? When he begged. What name did he use? Your fucking name. Which one?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna, I don't remember every— Dante called me Trouble. He stared at her. Miss Trouble if he was happy. Mrs. Trouble when I was mad at him. He'd come in and say, Mrs. Trouble, I fucked up, and I'd know I had to sit down before that nigga finished talking. She laughed, and that made Red angrier than anything she'd said. She couldn't help it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She was remembering Dante coming into their little apartment with a whole bumper in his hands. He'd taken it off the car he'd borrowed for their honeymoon. He'd brought the bumper upstairs because he thought she might be less mad if he hadn't left any of it behind. Nigga carried it like flowers, she told me later. She laughed then too.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I hated the dead nigga for making her laugh with something he'd done years before I met her, and I wanted to hear it again anyway. In Red's room, she wiped her eyes with the back of her wrist. You don't know how he talked to me. I know what he was. Then talk about that. Talk about your dead nigga.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You don't get to talk about mine. Red came close enough that she could smell the drink. You keep making him a saint. No. I'm remembering my husband. That nigga stole money, lied badly, and left his socks in the bed. I loved him. You think telling me he was a bad man changes something? She touched the watch again.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tell me something I don't fucking know. That nigga Dante said the same shit, Red went on. A house. A different life. Music. That nigga was gonna buy you a microphone and call himself a husband. Shawna turned back. That nigga was my husband. I paid for the wedding. You paid for the room. I paid for everything. Then you should've kept the receipts.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Maybe the preacher would've married you. Red threw the glass. It hit the wall beside the horse and broke. Shawna said she didn't move, which she was proud of until she told me why. Her legs had gone stiff. She couldn't move. He came toward her. You used to know how to talk to me. I used to need you to stop talking.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He caught her face in one hand. That's where the picture came from. He called one of his men in and told him to take it while he held her there. Shawna stared into the phone. He'll see you touching me, she said. That's the point. I know. The man took the picture and left.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Red's ring dragged against the edge of her jaw when he let go. She looked at it. You wearing it now? His hand closed. Wearing what? All that money, and you still want somebody to notice. He put his hand in his pocket. A telephone rang outside the room, and Red's face changed when the man at the door told him who was calling. Frost?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna asked. Red looked at her. She knew the name. Had heard it in enough penthouse conversations to recognize which uniform Red meant when he said the city would be reasonable. The man at the door whispered something. Red took the phone so hard the man stepped backward. What do you mean arrested? Shawna leaned back in the white chair.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, when she told me this part later, she made me listen twice. Said the first time I'd smiled so much I hadn't heard the whole sentence. Red kept listening. Knox said what? Shawna lifted her cigarette. My captain? He covered the phone. Shut up. I'm just wondering which nigga finally made your policeman nervous. He went into the hallway to finish the call.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Left the door open three inches. Left the man who'd taken the picture inside with her. The man looked tired. Thirty-eight, name of Arlo, a little gray beginning in his beard. She knew him too. He'd once carried her groceries upstairs when the elevator broke and then apologized because Red heard him asking whether she was all right.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You don't have to stand in here, she told him. He looked at the door. It's my job. Nigga, your job's turning into a funeral. He didn't answer. She stood up with the cigarette in one hand. He moved toward her. She lifted the other hand as if she only wanted him to stop crowding her.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then she threw the heavy silver cigarette box into his face. Arlo went back against the wall. She ran through the door, past Red with the telephone still against his ear, and into the corridor before either man understood that waiting quietly had ended. Red shouted her name. She kept running. Her borrowed dress caught the corner of a table.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She pulled free and left a strip of blue silk behind her. At the far end, the service doors were open. Light came through from a stairwell. She could hear men below, radios, a woman crying. She hit the door with her shoulder and nearly fell over a waiter sitting on the landing. He was holding his wrist. Blood marked his white cuff.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Beside him stood a young-looking woman who told Shawna she was twenty-four when Shawna asked if she could lift him. Both of them had been trying to get past the men downstairs. Where's the outside door? Shawna asked. Two floors, the woman said. But they won't let us— Get him up. They lifted the waiter together. Shawna took his good side.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The woman took the other. They started down the stairs, three people moving awkwardly, the blue dress dragging through dust and somebody else's dropped flowers. Behind them, Red came through the service door. Shawna! She didn't look back. Nigga, if you want to help, get his fucking feet. Red caught her at the next landing. The woman with the waiter stopped.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He pointed toward the stairs below. You two. Go. They stared. Go! Shawna held on to the waiter until the woman had him steady. Then she let them pass. She watched them reach the lower door, watched the woman look up at her once, watched them disappear into the light. Red grabbed her arm. You made me run. You should try it more.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He pulled her toward him. Think you're him now? She looked at his hand, then his face. Nigga, I know exactly who I am. That's what's upsetting you. He tried to drag her back up the stairs. She planted her feet and hit him with Dante's watch across the wrist holding her. He swore and loosened his grip.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She drove an elbow into his chest, got one step away, and nearly reached the lower door. Arlo stood in it. One eye was swelling. Blood ran from his nose. He looked at Shawna, looked at Red behind her, and for one second she thought he might move. Then he raised his gun. She stopped.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He couldn't make himself look at her while he pointed it. I'm sorry, he said. Then get better at it. Red pulled her back upstairs. Her shoulder struck the rail. She bit the inside of her cheek to keep from giving him a sound he could enjoy. When he put her back into the white chair, the room looked different.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The cigarette box lay on the floor. The little patch of carpet where it had stood was clean and bright amid the mess. Red bent over her. You get one more fucking idea— She looked up at him. I got several. You're gonna need a longer night. He stepped away. Shawna told me her hands were shaking after that.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She put them under her thighs so he wouldn't see. She had failed to get out. Two other people had made it. She held on to that while he paced in front of her. When I asked what she'd been thinking, she put her feet beneath my leg and looked at me like the answer ought to have been obvious.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: What my nigga would've done, she said. Only in a better dress. At the house, I didn't know any of this yet. Marcellus was still looking at the same photograph, holding my phone so close to his face I thought he might press his forehead through it. It's the stone, he said. Nigga, tell me you sure. Yes. Nigga, we were sure at the party.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He looked at me over the top of the phone. You were. I wanted to throw him through the rest of the door. I also wanted him to be right more than I'd wanted anything besides hearing her voice. Tell me, I said. He set the decoy on the table. In that room it looked worth forty million dollars. It looked worth killing for.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Red could've shown it to a king, and the king would've started moving money. Marcellus looked at it like an old sin. Nigga changed the setting on the original. Put dark stones around it. Made it look smaller by giving you other things to see. Nigga, you can read forty million through my phone? I can tell you he didn't do a good job.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: His hands had steadied. For the first time that night, he was somewhere he'd spent more years than prison. He turned the picture toward the light. I saw the ring at the gala. Only from the side. I thought I recognized the shoulder of the mounting. Here. He touched the screen. The nigga kept that part. Because it's gold? Tank asked.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Because that nigga's an idiot. Rosa let out a breath through her nose. Finally, some good fucking news. Marcellus showed us where the blue metal curved under the stone. Not a secret map. Not a number to somebody's money. The old curve of a mounting he had shaped himself. Red had reused one tiny part when he changed the necklace into a ring.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Marcellus knew the work the way I knew the sound of Shawna coming down our stairs. He has her stone under his finger, he said. Nobody spoke for a moment. Then I said, We'll get it. He looked at me. Will we, my nigga? Say the whole promise. Yeah. If that nigga says her or the diamond? Her.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I didn't wait to see how that felt to him. If that nigga says burn the letter? I burn it. If he says give him back the proof of what he did? Then he gets it. You want me to make you a promise, I'll make you one. I'm bringing her home. Everything else better find a way to come with us. Marcellus nodded.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: His mouth tightened once. Dante said something very much like that. I grabbed the edge of the table. Nigga, I'm not Dante. I know. Then stop putting that nigga between me and every fucking thing I do. Rosa said my name. I shook my head. No. I love her. Right now. Me. I'm the nigga standing here bleeding. I'm the nigga going out there.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You can remember him all you want, but when her phone rings, I want her to know who's calling. My voice had gone loud enough to shake. I hated all three of them hearing it. Marcellus took the papers we had brought out of the gala and laid them beside Celeste's old letter.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Rosa handed him the original order from Dante's watch, still inside its envelope. He kept the different pages apart. One held a dead woman's handwriting. The others held proof that Red had wanted another man dead. They'd cost more nights than I could count, and I would have set them all on fire if it got Shawna through that door.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then give her something to answer, he said. He slid my phone back to me. I opened her name. The last message I'd sent before the gala was still there. You look good as fuck. She had sent back a picture of one eye, half her forehead, and her middle finger.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She'd been trying to take a photograph of the whole dress and got mad at the phone. I stared until the screen blurred. Rosa stood beside me. She sent me six of those, she said quietly. Bitch got the bathroom ceiling in one. I wiped my face with the heel of my hand. Nigga, I whispered, though I wasn't talking to anybody now.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I started typing. I'm coming. Wear whatever you want. Then I deleted the second sentence. She couldn't choose what she was wearing. She couldn't choose where she was sitting. Red would read it first, and I wanted to take his head off for being between us even inside a fucking phone. I sent only the first two words.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: At the Saint, Shawna said Red watched the message arrive. He held the phone where she could see it and smiled. Nigga thinks he's in a love song. Then don't stand in the chorus. He took the phone away. She asked for her purse. He laughed at that.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She asked for water instead, and he brought it because he wanted to look like the kind of man who brought water. Tell me you were lying to that nigga, he said. She drank. About what? All of it. That's a lot of lying. You lied to Valentino. She set the glass down. Yeah. You lied to me. Yeah.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then tell me you lied to that nigga. He waited so hard that Shawna could see him believing her before she even opened her mouth. She said that was the ugliest thing in the room. He'd hurt her, trapped her, scared her, and still wanted her to make his heart feel better. She almost gave him what he wanted. Not because it was true.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Because she knew how to do it. She knew exactly how soft to make her voice. She could've called him baby and watched his shoulders come down. Instead she said, I told Aiden I wasn't scared. Red leaned closer. There you go. I told him I didn't think about Dante when we were together. He smiled. And?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I told him I didn't like that stupid fucking cross. You see? You see what I'm saying? She looked straight at him. I told him I could live without him. His smile went away. She said his name then. Not mine. Red's. She wanted him to know he was the one hearing it. That was a lie. He knocked the water out of her hand.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: For a second she thought he was going to hit her again. He stood there breathing, staring at the wet front of her dress. Then he picked up his jacket. Get up. Where? You wanna see your nigga so bad, let's go see him. He opened her purse and took out the little silver pistol.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He looked at it, then at her, and put it in his jacket. Taking this too, he said. He took her back into the hall. She left the cigarette burning in his silver box. She told me that part twice. Of everything he'd taken away from her that night, she wanted me to know he'd forgotten to make her put it out.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: At ten thirty-seven, he sent me another message. On our way. Don't disappoint her. I looked around the room at Tank, Rosa, Marcellus, and the three million dollars that had already buried too many people. Call everybody, I said. Tank picked up his phone. Everybody? Everybody who ever called me brother.
